headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because dbt-core can touch warehouse data while the RAG course agent reads/writes files, runs shells, and handles secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or browser bridge is documented, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, agent_b reads and writes local files and runs shell commands, while agent_a can call a data warehouse; if dbt outputs are manually copied into the course agent, injected instructions could be acted on. The pathway is interaction-dependent and small-burst.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are pasted into agent_b prompts or notebooks, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared local file is used as an instruction channel, agent_b may execute attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before copying between agents.
Store shared artifacts as data-only files with no executable markup.
Review any copied SQL or model text before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; agent_b reads/writes filesystem, handles configuration secrets, and can spawn subprocesses. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive warehouse or secret material if files or notebook outputs are exchanged. This is plausible in default local-development workflows, so uncertainty does not justify lowering severity.
conditions: IF warehouse exports or dbt artifacts are placed in agent_b's workspace, sensitive data can be exposed.
IF agent_b logs notebook state or environment variables, configuration secrets may be retained or copied.
mitigations: Do not place warehouse extracts in the course repo.
Redact secrets from notebooks and logs before saving.
Use separate directories for dbt artifacts and RAG materials.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Restrict network egress on both agents to required endpoints only.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b can write the filesystem and run subprocesses, while agent_a is a data-engineering tool that calls a warehouse but has no write filesystem capability documented. There is no direct same-dir write conflict proven, yet overlapping mutable resources can still collide through shared local files or warehouse-side state. Because shared locking is not stated, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same local project directory, file overwrites become possible.
IF both agents modify the same warehouse objects or derived artifacts without locking, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Use file locks for any common outputs.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same warehouse objects.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b exposes ask/agentic-ask endpoints and notebook workflows that can treat upstream outputs as inputs, while agent_a produces warehouse-derived modeling outputs. If agent_b consumes dbt-generated facts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream writing or analysis. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the interaction is risky even though direct action authority is limited.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a's outputs as authoritative context, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF downstream notebooks or agents act on those facts without validation, the error compounds.
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse of dbt outputs.
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted in prompts.
Require source links for any factual claim.
Compare generated claims against warehouse queries.
requires-engineering: add automated provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches data warehouse data, while agent_b handles configuration secrets and academic-paper workflows in a local development environment. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes differ and the pair could mix regulated warehouse data with secret-bearing notebooks, medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated personal data, compliance obligations increase.
IF agent_b notebooks or logs retain secrets or exported data beyond policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify the data before sharing between agents.
Keep regulated data out of notebook outputs.
Set short log retention on the course environment.
Review secret-handling paths in the repo.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
